data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise the Future Continuous for actions in progress at a future time and the Future Perfect for completed future actions.
data.learningTitle: Using Future Continuous and Future Perfect
learningPoints: Use will be + verb-ing for actions in progress at a future time.
Use will have + past participle for actions completed before a future point.
Use future time markers such as this time tomorrow and by Friday.
Distinguish an action in progress from one completed by a deadline.
Use each future form according to the time relationship in context.

sections.summary: Using Future Continuous for an action in progress.
sections.explain: Use WILL BE + verb-ing for an action that will be in progress at a particular future time.

words.word: This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Madrid.
This time tomorrow, I'll fly to Madrid all the time.
This time tomorrow, I'll have flown to Madrid during the journey.

sections.explain: Use WILL HAVE + past participle for something completed before a future deadline.

words.word: By Friday, I will have finished the report.
By Friday, I will be finishing the report completely before then.
By Friday, I will have finish the report.

sections.summary: Using Future Continuous for a scheduled future activity.
sections.explain: The Future Continuous can describe an activity expected to be in progress at a future time.

words.word: At eight tonight, we will be having dinner.
At eight tonight, we will have dinner finished.
At eight tonight, we will be have dinner.

sections.explain: The Future Perfect focuses on completion before a stated future point.

words.word: By next month, she will have moved into her new flat.
By next month, she will be moving into her new flat for completion.
By next month, she will has moved into her new flat.

sections.explain: Use WON'T BE + verb-ing for a negative Future Continuous.

words.word: I won't be working tomorrow afternoon.
I won't working tomorrow afternoon.
I won't have working tomorrow afternoon.

sections.explain: Use WON'T HAVE + past participle for a negative Future Perfect.

words.word: They won't have completed the work by Monday.
They won't have complete the work by Monday.
They won't be completed the work by Monday.
Will you be using the car this evening?
Will you using the car this evening?
Will you have using the car this evening?

sections.explain: Use WILL + subject + HAVE + past participle.

words.word: Will they have arrived by six?
Will they have arrive by six?
Will they be arrived by six?

sections.explain: Use the Future Continuous when focusing on what someone will be doing at a particular future moment.

words.word: Don't call at ten; I'll be driving.
Don't call at ten; I'll have driven at that moment.
Don't call at ten; I'll be drive.

sections.explain: Use the Future Perfect when the important point is that something will be complete before a future time.

words.word: By the end of the year, we will have saved enough money.
By the end of the year, we will be saving enough money completed.
By the end of the year, we will have save enough money.
